answer: What survives to the raven is a record of labour, not a list of addresses. The lantern holds work receipts rather than names, so the mesa of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. Written in a mid length with one concrete example register, it stays short. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts, re-queued for a second panel, the unit of trust is a task, not an address.
